Electricity runs through conductive elements via sparks, and players build working logic gates, engines, and nuclear reactors from them. Element count passed 250 by 2025; the source is GPLv3 and the in-game save browser is the main distribution channel for builds.

name: The Sims
summary: A life sim in which the player builds a house and guides a household of Sims whose decaying motives, personalities, careers, and relationships produce an open-ended domestic story.
core_loop: build and furnish the lot -> motives decay -> objects advertise motive gains and Sims act or take queued orders -> jobs pay for upgrades -> skills and friendships unlock promotions -> expand house and family
design_notes: Will Wright drew on Christopher Alexander's A Pattern Language, treating a house as a set of functional patterns judged by how well they serve the people living in it. Much of the behavioral logic sits in objects: each object advertises which motives it raises and by how much, and Sims with free will enabled choose among those advertisements weighted by their current motives. Sims are deliberately not fully autonomous, since paying bills, finding jobs, exercising, and having children need explicit commands, so the player alternates between architect and caretaker. Build and Buy modes pause time, separating spatial design from the live simulation.

name: The Sims 2
summary: The 3D sequel to The Sims that adds aging through seven life stages, genetic inheritance, aspirations with wants and fears, and memories, so households play across generations.
core_loop: create a household with aspirations -> wants and fears roll -> direct Sims to meet motives and wants -> aspiration meter and memories shift -> Sims age, marry, and have children who inherit genes -> continue with the next generation
design_notes: The Sims 2 turns the household sandbox into a generational one: babies become toddlers after 3 days, toddlers children after 4, children teens after 8, teens adults after 15, and adults elders after 29, and an elder's remaining life depends on the aspiration meter at the time of aging. Children inherit appearance and personality from both parents through dominant and recessive genes, and each Sim's aspiration (one of eight, such as Romance, Family, Knowledge, or Popularity) biases which wants and fears appear. The wants-and-fears panel is a short-horizon goal generator with no mechanic id yet (proposed as aspiration-wants). SimPE and Body Shop made behavior hacks and custom genetics routine in its mod community.

name: The Sims 3
summary: The third mainline Sims game, which places households in a seamless open neighborhood where unplayed Sims keep living, and replaces personality sliders with up to five traits and mood with stacked moodlets.
core_loop: pick traits and a lifetime wish -> moodlets from events stack into mood -> wishes and opportunities appear -> act across the open town -> earn Lifetime Happiness for rewards -> story progression advances other households
design_notes: Neighborhoods are seamless worlds, so Sims walk between lots without loading screens on PC, and Story Progression keeps households the player is not controlling aging, working, and forming relationships. Personality is a set of up to five discrete traits that unlock and bias interactions, and mood is the sum of moodlets, timed modifiers with named causes. Fulfilled wishes pay Lifetime Happiness points spent on Lifetime Rewards, replacing the wants and fears of The Sims 2. Off-screen story progression and wish generation are captured by the offscreen-life-progression and aspiration-wants mechanics.

name: The Sims 4
summary: The fourth mainline Sims game, built around a dominant emotion computed from moodlets, three-trait personalities with aspiration rewards, multitasking, room-based building, and an in-game Gallery for sharing creations.
core_loop: build a home or download one from the Gallery -> moodlets from events and surroundings set the dominant emotion -> emotion unlocks interactions and speeds skills -> pursue aspiration milestones and a career -> earn rewards -> share households and builds
design_notes: The Sims 4 makes emotion the central state: moodlets from actions, events, objects, and social interactions carry an emotion type and weight, and the strongest set the Sim's single dominant emotion, which gates emotional interactions and speeds matching skills. Adult personality is three traits plus a bonus trait from the chosen aspiration, and completing aspiration milestones grants reward traits. Build mode treats rooms as units that can be moved, duplicated, saved to a library, and shared through the Gallery; the base game became free to play on 2022-10-18. Neighborhood Stories, a free update that advances unplayed households, is the offscreen-life-progression mechanic.

name: Theme Hospital
summary: A hospital management game where the player builds rooms, hires and trains staff, and routes patients with comic diseases through diagnosis and treatment to meet level goals.
core_loop: build rooms from blueprints -> hire and train staff -> patients queue for GP diagnosis and referrals -> treatment cures or kills -> fees and reputation -> research new rooms and meet level goals
design_notes: Theme Hospital turns medicine into routing. The GP and specialist diagnosis rooms raise a patient's diagnosis certainty, and the player sets the threshold at which treatment starts (it can be set above 100%), trading throughput against deaths from wrong cures. Rooms are fixed blueprints that need set furniture and, for some, specialist staff, so the staff roster and the floor plan gate each other. Machines that explode without a handyman, epidemics that can be covered up before the health inspector arrives, and timed emergencies add pressure on top of the queues. Much of the code came from Theme Park; CorsixTH is an open-source reimplementation with a level editor.

name: Theme Park
summary: A theme park management game in which the player builds rides and shops, tunes prices and recipes for individually simulated visitors, and sells parks to expand worldwide.
core_loop: place rides, shops, and paths -> visitors arrive by bus and choose attractions -> tune prices and shop ingredients -> fund research and hire staff -> yearly judging against rivals -> sell the park and buy a plot abroad
design_notes: Theme Park gives every visitor its own record (about 200 bytes each) and lets the player change the product as well as its price: ingredient settings such as sugar in ice cream trade cost against whether customers return. The full-simulation level adds wage and supply negotiations, where failure means staff strikes or lost shipments, plus research funding and shares; the sandbox level removes them, so one engine serves three depths. Unhappy visitors attract thugs, which ties satisfaction to crime. Negotiation has no mechanic in the taxonomy (proposed as negotiation).

name: This War of Mine
summary: A survival sim about civilians in a besieged city who maintain a shelter by day, scavenge by night, and face moral choices that change their mood until a randomized ceasefire.
core_loop: spend the day in the shelter crafting, cooking, trading, and treating -> assign night roles -> one survivor scavenges a location -> encounters force moral choices -> hunger, wounds, illness, and mood shift -> survive until the ceasefire
design_notes: The game turns war into a resource-and-conscience problem: survival needs push the player toward theft or violence, and those acts lower survivors' mood, so material and moral states are coupled. A day-night split separates base management (snipers keep survivors inside by day) from risky scavenging by one chosen survivor, and the length of the war is randomized so the player cannot plan to a known end. The radio reports weather, prices, and war news that let the player anticipate shortages. It draws on the 1992-96 Siege of Sarajevo.

name: Timberborn
summary: A city builder for beaver colonies in which simulated water flows over terrain, recurring droughts and toxic badtides cut or poison it, and players dam, channel, and store water while building upward.
core_loop: dam and channel rivers -> irrigate farms and forests from stored water -> beavers work, eat, and seek wellbeing -> a drought or badtide cuts or poisons the flow -> stockpiles and reservoirs carry the colony through -> build upward and expand
design_notes: Water is a simulated field rather than a resource count: a 2D model adapted from erosion simulation linked each tile to four neighbors by virtual pipes and was replaced by 3D water in Update 6 (October 2024), so dams, floodgates, and canals change where moisture reaches crops. Recurring droughts grow harsher and badtides turn sources into contaminating badwater, so play alternates between building reservoirs and surviving a known dry period. Limited space pushes housing and workshops into vertical stacks, and sensors and relays let players automate floodgates.

name: Tiny Glade
summary: A medieval building sandbox in which drawn walls, paths, and building outlines are assembled by procedural rules into detailed castles and cottages, with no goals, management, or failure states.
core_loop: draw walls, paths, and building outlines -> procedural rules assemble bricks, roofs, doors, and supports to fit -> reshape terrain and add water -> ivy grows and sheep wander the paths -> keep editing
design_notes: Tiny Glade takes the Townscaper approach to freehand strokes: a path drawn through a building produces a door, and raising a building adds columns and beams to support it, so local rules respond to how elements meet. The two-person studio built it on a custom fork of the Rust engine Bevy. It is a boundary case: the only autonomous elements are ambient life such as growing ivy and wandering sheep.

name: Tomodachi Life
summary: A Nintendo 3DS life sim in which player-made Mii characters live in an island apartment building, form friendships, quarrels, and romances on their own, and ask the player to solve their problems.
core_loop: add Miis to the apartment -> Miis develop friendships, crushes, and quarrels -> they raise problems such as food, clothes, or advice -> solve problems to fill happiness and earn money -> level-up gifts and new island venues unlock -> couples marry and have children
design_notes: The player is an omnipotent observer who cannot control Miis directly and instead answers their requests, so most of the comedy comes from autonomous pairings and quarrels among Miis whose looks, names, voices, and personalities the player designed. Key relationship changes pass through player consent: the player approves a confession before it happens and resolves fights indirectly. The apartment holds up to 100 Miis, and a filled happiness meter levels a Mii up and earns it a present, so care is paced by a stream of small templated problems rather than decaying meters.

name: Townscaper
summary: A town-building toy in which clicking colored blocks onto an irregular grid lets a wave function collapse solver assemble houses, arches, stairways, bridges, and gardens, with no goals or resources.
core_loop: click to add or remove a colored block on the irregular grid -> the solver picks modules for that cell and its neighbors -> arches, stairs, roofs, and gardens appear -> keep editing
design_notes: The grid is a subdivided, jittered hex grid of irregular quads, and each edit triggers a real-time wave function collapse that narrows the valid corner modules for the changed cells and their neighbors before decoration is applied. The player expresses only occupancy and color; all architectural detail is derived, which makes the game a pure case of procedural build assist. It is a boundary case because nothing evolves without the player; its author calls it more of a toy than a game.

name: Transport Tycoon
summary: A transport business sim in which the player builds road, rail, sea, and air networks between towns and industries over a century, earning by delivery speed and distance while vehicles age and break down.
core_loop: survey towns and industries -> build stations, track, roads, docks, and airports -> give vehicles order lists -> payment by cargo, distance, and delivery time -> station ratings and towns grow -> replace aging vehicles and expand
design_notes: Transport Tycoon extends Railroad Tycoon to four transport modes on one isometric map and makes cargo value decay with transit time, so mail suits short or fast routes while coal keeps its value over long hauls. Stations only collect from nearby towns and industries, and a station rating decides how much of an industry's output it receives, which rewards frequent, fast service. Vehicles lose reliability with age and new models arrive on a timeline from 1930 to 2030 (1950 to 2050 in Deluxe), so the fleet must be renewed; date-driven model availability is proposed as dated-tech-timeline. Town councils rate each company through the Local Authority system, which can block new stations. OpenTTD, a reverse-engineered reimplementation first released in 2004, continues the design.

name: Tropico 6
summary: A political city builder in which El Presidente develops an island archipelago across four eras while individually simulated citizens' happiness and faction loyalties decide elections, protests, and revolts.
core_loop: build housing, jobs, and services across the islands -> each citizen's happiness and faction alignment shift with conditions -> issue edicts, trade, and raid to fund the treasury -> advance through four eras -> win elections or suppress rebels to stay in power
design_notes: Tropico couples a conventional production and services city builder to a political layer: each simulated citizen holds happiness and faction alignments, and those aggregate into election results and rebel recruitment. Edicts and policies trade one faction's approval against another's, so building decisions double as political ones. Tropico 6 moves play to an archipelago joined by bridges from the World Wars era onward and organizes progress into Colonial, World Wars, Cold War, and Modern eras.

name: Two Point Hospital
summary: A hospital management game and spiritual successor to Theme Hospital in which the player builds rooms, trains staff with traits and qualifications, and cures comic illnesses across a chain of hospitals.
core_loop: build and decorate rooms -> hire staff with traits and train qualifications -> patients flow from GP to diagnosis to treatment -> cures earn money and reputation -> research and Kudosh unlock items -> earn stars to open the next hospital
design_notes: Two Point Hospital keeps Theme Hospital's room-blueprint and diagnosis-pipeline structure and adds a deeper staff layer: every hire has personality traits, a specialisation, and trainable qualifications, so the training room is a second production line beside the clinical one. Room prestige rises with room size and decoration and feeds staff happiness, which links interior design to staff retention. Progress spreads across many hospitals with one-to-three-star goals, and items unlock with Kudosh, a currency earned from challenges rather than money. Assistants can run marketing campaigns (proposed mechanic advertising-awareness).

name: Ultima Online
summary: A persistent fantasy MMO in which players progress through skills without classes or levels, craft goods for a player-driven economy, own persistent houses, and could attack each other anywhere until the 2000 split into Trammel and Felucca.
core_loop: practice skills by using them -> gather resources and craft goods -> trade with other players -> build and furnish a house -> fight monsters or other players -> recover from death and re-equip
design_notes: Ultima Online tried to simulate a world rather than a set of classes: skills grow with practice, goods come from player crafting, and houses persist on the map. Its planned artificial-life ecology, in which animal behavior responded to ecological events, was removed during beta because players killed creatures faster than they could spawn. Unrestricted player killing at launch led to the 2000 Trammel and Felucca split into consensual and open PvP facets, an early rule-zoned world (proposal pvp-security-zones); fans later reverse-engineered it to build server emulators.

name: Universe Sandbox
summary: A space physics sandbox where the player builds and alters star systems and watches Newtonian n-body gravity, collisions, and simplified planetary climate play out at adjustable speed.
core_loop: load or build a system -> set masses, positions, and time step -> run gravity forward -> watch orbits, collisions, and climate respond -> tweak parameters or add bodies
design_notes: Every body attracts every other under Newtonian n-body gravity, so the player can test questions such as what happens if a star passes the Solar System and see the answer rather than read it. The current version (a rewrite released as Universe Sandbox 2 in 2014 and renamed in 2018, still in early access) adds composition from a small set of materials, collisions that leave molten craters, and a climate layer where sea ice tracks axial tilt and oceans boil near a star. The simulation is an instrument for parameter sweeps; there are no goals or agents.

name: Utopia
summary: A two-player Intellivision strategy game in which rival island rulers spend gold on buildings and boats in timed rounds, scoring points for how well their populations are housed, fed, and kept content.
core_loop: spend gold on houses, farms, factories, forts, and boats -> round timer runs while boats fish and clouds rain on farms -> end-of-round income and score from population welfare -> rebels, storms, and pirates strike -> next round
design_notes: Utopia runs as up to 50 real-time rounds of 30 to 120 seconds, so the turn boundary is a clock rather than a player action; income from factories arrives at round end while fishing and rain income depend on what happens during the round. Two players share one screen with no AI opponent, and each can fund rebels on the other's island or sink the other's fishing boat with a PT boat, so the welfare score is contested directly. It is commonly cited as the first city-building game, though its release year is disputed between 1981 and 1982.

name: Valheim
summary: A co-op Viking survival game in a seeded procedural world of biomes where players gather, build structurally supported shelters, eat for stat buffs, and defeat biome bosses to progress.
core_loop: explore seeded biomes -> gather wood, stone, and ore -> build shelters that must be supported and roofed -> eat food for health and stamina -> craft better gear -> summon and defeat each biome's boss -> sail to harder biomes
design_notes: Food is a reward rather than a punishment: eating raises maximum health and stamina and speeds regeneration, and there is no starvation, so the survival layer pushes players toward better food rather than threatening death. This consumable-buff model does not fit survival-meters cleanly (proposal filed). Building uses a support model in which stability falls with distance from the ground, so architecture follows material limits, and uncovered wood decays to half durability in rain. Progression is gated by eight bosses, each summoned with an offering. Early access began in February 2021 and 1.0 shipped in September 2026.

name: Versu
summary: A 2013 iPad interactive story platform from Linden Lab in which the player controls one character among autonomous agents who choose actions by simulating their outcomes against hundreds of desires within authored social practices.
core_loop: choose a character and episode -> practices offer actions for the situation -> player acts or waits -> other agents simulate each option and take the best for their desires -> emotions, evaluations, and relationships update -> the episode reaches an outcome
design_notes: Richard Evans and Emily Short built Versu around social practices: recurring situations such as a meal or a conversation written as reactive joint plans that offer actions to participants without controlling them. Each agent tests a candidate action by applying it to the world state, scoring the result against its desires (over 300 in total), and undoing it, which the authors contrast with the estimated consequences used in The Sims. World state is a set of exclusion-logic sentences, and the Praxis language with a stress tester that runs hundreds of simulated instances supported over 1,000 parameterized actions. Linden Lab cancelled the project in early 2014; social practices have no mechanic id and are proposed as social-practices.

name: Victoria 3
summary: An economic grand strategy game set from 1836 to 1936 in which the player industrializes a nation by building production chains, passing laws through interest-group politics, and pursuing diplomatic plays while population strata respond through wages, needs, and radicalism.
core_loop: queue construction of buildings -> buildings hire pops and run production methods -> goods trade at shifting market prices -> wages and needs set standard of living and interest-group support -> enact laws and pursue diplomatic plays -> expand industry
design_notes: Victoria 3 moves the player's main lever from units to the economy: the player queues construction and sets laws, and pops, prices, and wages respond, while armies are handled by generals assigned to fronts. Politics is an output of economics, since pops' economic status sets their interest-group affiliation and political strength. Diplomatic plays turn war declaration into a timed escalation of demands and counter-demands with a chance to back down (proposal crisis-escalation).

name: Viva Piñata
summary: A garden sim in which the player shapes terrain, plants, and water to attract 60 piñata species, then meets each species' requirements to make them residents, breed them, and manage the predators among them.
core_loop: dig, plant, and water the garden -> species outlines appear when appear requirements are met -> resident requirements turn visitors into residents -> residents meet romance requirements and lay eggs -> predators and sours disrupt -> sell or trade piñatas -> attract new species
design_notes: Viva Piñata turns habitat suitability into a readable checklist: each species has staged appear, visit, resident, and romance requirements, shown as a black-and-white outline that fills in when residency is met. Because piñatavores must eat other piñatas to become residents or breed, attracting one species can consume another, so the garden is a hand-built food web the player tunes by fencing, spacing, and timing. Sours and Professor Pester's ruffians supply authored pressure, and romance requirements can be bypassed with candy once a species has bred, trading early difficulty for collection speed.

name: Where Winds Meet
summary: An open-world martial-arts RPG whose NPCs answer free-text and voice chat through a live language model, included as an early large-audience deployment of runtime LLM characters.
core_loop: explore the open world -> talk to NPCs in free text or voice -> take quests and fights -> build reputation and skills -> explore further
design_notes: Included as a boundary case for natural-language interaction at scale. The Steam AI disclosure describes NPC text and voice chat generated in real time from player input. The main questline and combat remain authored and rule-based, so the language model sits beside the simulation rather than inside its state.

name: Whispers from the Star
summary: A voice-driven sci-fi narrative game in which the player helps stranded astronaut Stella survive on the planet Gaia through open-ended spoken or typed conversation answered by an AI-generated, voiced performance.
core_loop: Stella calls, texts, or sends voice messages about her situation -> player answers by voice or text -> model generates her spoken reply and choice -> her choices change whether she survives the situation -> story advances
design_notes: At runtime a model generates Stella's side of every exchange: the player's microphone or text input is answered with dialogue and a fully voiced performance that Anuttacon says was created in collaboration with an actor, with safety filters screening output. The store page says there is no script and that the player's words shape her choices and her survival, so advice acts as an indirect control on an agent the player cannot command. The surrounding structure is linear and story-driven per its store tags, which makes it a hybrid of authored situations and generated conversation. Anuttacon was formed in late 2023 by miHoYo co-founder Cai Haoyu, and this is its first game. It is a boundary case: the only simulated state is the conversation and Stella's choices.

name: Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic
summary: A planned-economy city builder in which every building, commodity, and citizen moves through explicit logistics, from construction materials delivered by truck to exports at border customs for rubles or dollars.
core_loop: set up construction offices and deliver materials to sites -> extract and process over 30 commodities by truck, rail, conveyor, and pipe -> house citizens near jobs and transit -> supply food, clothing, heat, and services to keep health, happiness, and loyalty -> export at customs for rubles or dollars -> import what the republic lacks
design_notes: Workers & Resources treats construction itself as logistics: buildings and roads need delivered concrete, steel, and prefab panels plus workers from the player's construction offices, or imported foreign labor at a cost, a system the taxonomy lacks (see run proposal). Over 30 commodities move by mode suited to their form (pipes and tanks for liquids, conveyors and trucks for ores, covered vehicles for goods), so freight network design is the main puzzle. Trade runs through East and West customs houses, flooding one bloc's market lowers returns, and heating demand rising in winter ties utilities to the calendar.

name: X-Plane
summary: A flight sim whose flight model computes forces on small elements of each wing, control surface, and propeller from aircraft geometry, used for entertainment and in FAA-approved training devices.
core_loop: pick or design an aircraft -> set location and weather -> fly by hand or autopilot -> blade-element forces respond to geometry and air -> land -> revise the aircraft in Plane Maker
design_notes: X-Plane uses blade element theory: wings, control surfaces, and propellers are split into elements and aerodynamic forces are computed on each from geometry, rather than looked up from performance tables, so an aircraft drawn in the bundled Plane Maker flies according to its shape. That approach underpins its use in FAA-approved training systems when paired with suitable hardware. A plugin SDK exposes simulator data for instruments, cockpits, and external hardware.

name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
summary: An open-world action adventure whose physics and chemistry engines let fire, wind, electricity, temperature, and material properties combine, so puzzles and fights accept solutions the designers did not script.
core_loop: spot a landmark -> climb, glide, or ride toward it under stamina limits -> solve shrines and fights with physics and elemental interactions -> gather and cook ingredients -> replace broken weapons -> push farther into the world
design_notes: The game is mostly authored content (map, shrines, story) and is included for its systemic layer. A modified Havok physics engine and a separate chemistry engine give objects material properties, so fire burns grass and creates updrafts, metal draws lightning and conducts electricity, wind carries flames and gliders, and cold or heat drains health unless countered by clothing or cooked food. Weapon durability and stamina force continual scavenging and route choice, and shrine puzzles accept any solution that satisfies the physical end condition.

name: Zoo Tycoon
summary: A zoo management game in which the player builds exhibits whose terrain, foliage, shelters, and toys must suit each species, balancing animal happiness against guest happiness and income.
core_loop: fence an exhibit -> match terrain, foliage, rocks, shelter, and toys to the species -> animals grow happy and breed -> guests visit, spend, and react -> awards and income -> research and adopt more animals
design_notes: Zoo Tycoon's core rule is exhibit suitability: each species reports how well its exhibit's terrain mix, foliage, rocks, shelters, toys, and keeper care match its needs, and that suitability drives animal happiness. Guest happiness depends on animal happiness, the species on show, buildings, and scenery, so the two satisfaction meters are chained. Failures are physical: incompatible species in one exhibit kill each other, fences decay, and escaped animals attack guests and staff. Too many complaints about unhappy animals block new adoptions until habitats are fixed.
